text:
alex_cs: FYI we have an escalation from a customer (internal ticket #4521). They say identical rerank payloads are returning different scores after yesterday's overnight model push. :eyes:

alex_cs: short repro they pasted:```json
{
  \"query\": \"best ergonomic keyboards\",
  \"candidates\": [\"k1\", \"k2\", \"k3\"]
}
```

alex_cs: two requests made 3s apart, same payload, different top score: 0.912 vs 0.846. Customer insists no retries or sharding in their client. Escalating to ML/infra to investigate.

deploy_bot: deploy completed: "rollout:model/pruned-v2" by maria_ml at 1758885600 -> target: 30% -> strategy: canary -> regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1.

maria_ml: thanks for the ping. We did push pruned-v2 overnight — weight pruning + a small kernel reorder to reduce memory. It was rolled as a canary 30% like the bot says. No intentional behavior changes to reranking loss, but pruning can change score calibration.

devon_eng: can you attach the raw request_id(s) and full HTTP logs? Need to confirm routing and which exact model the requests hit. Also please include model_version from response metadata.

alex_cs: pasted sanitized sample logs:```
[1758888999] req_id=abc123 route=/v1/rerank model=pruned-v2 score=0.912
[1758889002] req_id=abc124 route=/v1/rerank model=pruned-v1 score=0.846
```

alex_cs: note the first hit pruned-v2 and second hit pruned-v1 (customer says both should be the same). They say both requests originated from same client region.

maria_ml: that explains a lot — different model variants will produce calibration shifts. But if we've routed one request to pruned-v2 and another to pruned-v1 for the same traffic cohort that's a routing/rollout bug. I pushed a config change yesterday to prefer pruned-v2 for eu-west-1, but it shouldn't flip between variants per request.

sam_ops: checked routing logs: traffic steering rule for acmecorp (customer tag c-acme) had a malformed priority so their sessions got split across canary and baseline during sticky-session fallback. Attaching flow:```
- incoming requests with cookie X -> route to sticky pool
- if sticky pool full -> fallback to round-robin across pool variants (pruned-v1, pruned-v2)
```

sam_ops: tl;dr: some of their requests hit pruned-v2, others pruned-v1. That explains identical payloads different scores. Working on a hotfix to enforce session stickiness for customers with rerank SLAs.

devon_eng: good catch. For mitigation: 1) recommend customer pin model_version=pruned-v1 in their request until we fix routing; 2) we'll roll back the canary for acme-specific routing. Can we get a reproducible curl they used so we can run in our env?

alex_cs: here's the curl they used:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{\"query\":\"best ergonomic keyboards\",\"candidates\":[\"k1\",\"k2\",\"k3\"],\"customer_id\":\"c-acme\"}'
```

maria_ml: I'll run a batch of identical requests against pruned-v1 and pruned-v2 in our staging harness and dump score distributions. If pruning consistently shifts scores, we should add a calibration layer or bump the threshold mapping in Optimize.

devon_eng: reproduction plan recorded: 1) replay their exact curl with pinned model_version header; 2) remove pin to observe routing variance; 3) capture model_version and score for 500 consecutive identical requests. Sam, can you enable a quick feature-flag to force stickiness for c-acme?

sam_ops: feature-flag enabled for c-acme -> sticky routing enforced in us-east-1 & eu-west-1. Rolling out across other regions in 10m.

alex_cs: customer notified: workaround to pin to pruned-v1 or wait ~15min for stickiness fix. They're OK with pin for now but asked for postmortem.

maria_ml: initial hypothesis: pruning changed score calibration and mixed routing caused observed delta. Action items: [maria_ml] run score drift eval and produce histogram + delta report; [devon_eng] fix rollout policy so canary doesn't split sessions; [sam_ops] verify rollout config validation to prevent malformed priority; [alex_cs] keep customer updated.

devon_eng: I'll also add an alert in Console for rerank request variance when same request_id pattern sees >5% score delta across identical payloads in 1m window.

alex_cs: thanks team. I'll collect the artifacts and open a postmortem doc once we have the evals. :thumbsup:
